strategy.summary:
Verbindungstechnik Mairhofer is a sound, family-owned fastener maker. It is deprioritising us: our spend is under one percent of its turnover, and it has said it will not extend individual agreements and will serve standard items from stock at list conditions. At the same time it has an idle second shift and has said it could take extra parts at short notice, so volume still matters to it.

Our position differs by part:
- part:360010 and part:360012 are dual-sourced with Leitner, which is markedly cheaper and has better ppm on both. That gives us real leverage.
- part:360011 is single-sourced, which is our exposure.

Cost drivers support only a small drift, below its pricing-committee threshold. History shows it settles far below its ask, and it has even cut prices.

The main game is keeping the framework, especially for part:360011, at current or near-current prices. To do that, offer bundled, growing, binding volume, a longer term and punctual payment. Use the Leitner price gap to cap or cut prices on the dual-sourced parts.

The dual-sourced parts carry a large premium over Leitner, and drivers justify only a small drift. It also cut prices last year, so on part:360010 and part:360012 there is room toward the benchmark backed by a quota shift.

part:360011 is single-source with no benchmark, so realistically aim to hold its price. The overriding risk is not price but losing the individual agreement; its low dependency on us means hard squeezing may simply push it to list terms.

strategy.writer_notes: Frame every message as a proposal to stay a worthwhile customer: a bundle of three growing parts, a binding volume commitment, a longer term and punctual payment, in return for keeping individual prices. On the bolt and the nut, use the cheaper approved second source to justify reducing or reallocating quota unless the price comes down. Stay matter-of-fact, without threats. Never signal dependency, and keep its price at current level. Address the late-payment issue proactively.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for any of the three parts, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured directly. The best proxy is the rival Leitner (sup:70610). It supplies M12x40 bolts at 12.46 against Mairhofer's 14.52, which is 14.2% lower. It supplies M12 nuts at 4.91 against 5.60, which is 12.3% lower. Leitner's prices have been flat since 2023. Mairhofer's price premium is therefore roughly 12-14% on the dual-sourced parts. The evidence is thin for M16x60 (360011), which has no benchmark.

The cost drivers do not justify a material increase. The fastener PPI rose 1.7% over 12 months and sits 1.2% below its 36-month peak. At a weight of about 0.6, that is worth roughly +1.0% on price. Labour rose 2.7% at a weight of 0.08-0.13, adding roughly +0.2-0.35%. The combined justified drift is about +1.2-1.4%, which is below the 2% threshold for their pricing committee. The 7.3% steel rise and the 48% copper rise in the news are not specific to fasteners and should not be accepted as drivers.

Price history since the last change:
- 360010 has been flat at 14.52 since 2023 and never passed on the lower index.
- 360011 moved 37.81, then 38.39, then 37.64 (-2% in 2026).
- 360012 moved 5.62, then 5.78, then 5.60 (-3.1% in 2026).
The 2026 cuts happened while the index was rising, which suggests margin buffer. Historically they settled 2.4-2.8 percentage points below their ask.

The new quotes (2026-09) simply restate current prices on 'list conditions, stock only' with 7-day validity. Together with the account refocus, this is a signal that they are withdrawing rather than pushing for an increase. Our pricing room depends mostly on whether they want the business at all. We are 0.7% of their turnover.

Room on price: the target is roughly 12.5-13.5 for 360010 and about 5.0-5.3 for 360012, moving toward the Leitner benchmark. The fallback is to shift quota to Leitner, which already holds 40% and 30% of these parts. For 360011, Mairhofer is the single source and owns the tooling, so the realistic goal is holding at 37.64 or accepting at most about +1%.

findings.text: Strategic deprioritisation of Hollerau: the sales director has said twice (Feb, May) that small accounts are under review, a new sales director called our volumes 'not strategic', and the supplier wrote that individual agreements will not be extended and that standard items will come from stock at list conditions. A press report confirms the refocus on key accounts. We are about 0.7% of its turnover (EUR 140k).

Contract ctr:4600070650 runs to 2026-12-31 and renews automatically unless terminated by 2026-11-01. Its e-mail signals that it may not want to renew individual terms. Price changes need 60 days' written notice before year end, so any increase for 2027 must be notified by about 2026-11-01. Both sides hold a clock.
Approval ladder: price changes above 2% need its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Expect asks at or below 2% that the key account manager can settle alone. Larger moves will be slow.

Contradictory signal of spare capacity: sales said in April that they could take additional parts at short notice and that the second shift has been on hold since spring. This means underutilisation, so volume and bundling are attractive to them despite the 'key account' rhetoric. Our forecasts are up 6-15% on all three parts.

Financially sound, family-owned company with 40 staff: equity ratio 39.8%, stable credit index 156, VDA 6.3 grade A. There is no distress, so it can afford to walk away from us. Cash pressure is not a lever.

Our payment behaviour is a sensitivity: 90.4% of invoices are paid late, on average 5.7 days late, and 16.7% more than 10 days late, on a contractual 30 days net. This gives them a legitimate complaint. Paying on time is a cheap concession to offer.

Its history weakens its position. It usually settles far below its ask, with prices flat or slightly down since 2023. A second source (Leitner) supplies 360010 and 360012 at 12-14% lower prices. Part 360011 is single-sourced, and the supplier owns the tooling on all parts.
It runs an operational holiday shutdown from 23 December to 6 January, with call-offs due by 10 December. Replies have become slower since the summer. Plan our timing accordingly.

findings.text: Framework agreement covers all three fasteners, runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice (by 2026-11-01). Prices are fixed per calendar year and any change needs written notice at least 60 days before year end (by ~2026-11-01). As of 2026-09 both the exit and the 2027 price notice window are still open.

The supplier has signalled it will not extend individual agreements and will serve standard items from stock at list conditions. It has repeatedly said Hollerau is 'not strategic'. The real risk is that it terminates or lets the framework lapse, not a normal price ask. Our spend is about EUR 140k/yr, roughly 0.7% of its EUR 19.5M turnover.

History: across 9 renewals it asked +0.5% to +5% and settled 0 pp to 2.8 pp below the ask. It settled at 0% in 5 of 9 and cut prices in 2026 on parts 360011 (-2%) and 360012 (-3.1%). Net prices since 2023 are flat to -0.4%. Asks above 2% need its pricing committee, which meets fortnightly.

Dependency differs by part. Parts 360010 (60/40) and 360012 (70/30) are dual-sourced with Leitner, whose current order prices are 14.2% and 12.3% below Mairhofer's. Mairhofer also won the 2025 benchmark RFQs. Part 360011 (M16x60) is single-sourced (100%) with no RFQ on record; this is our exposure. Tooling is listed n/a in sourcing, so the library's 'it owns the tooling' claim is doubtful for standard ISO parts.

Contract terms are payment 30 days net (below our 60-day standard), DAP, 7-day lead time, a 95% on-time target and EUR 150 per complaint. Actual on-time delivery is 84.1%, below target. We pay 5.7 days late on average, which weakens our hand on performance points.

findings.text: Delivery is weak but improving: rolling OTD 84.1% to 2026-09 (from 75.0% a year earlier, 73.4% low in 2024Q4), still far below the 95% contract target and about level with peers' median 84.6%. Late lines average 12.5 days late, max 32. part:360010 is worst (76.7% on time); part:360011 is rarely late (92%) but very late when it is (avg 27 days).

Quality is flat at roughly 235-296 ppm for three years (296 ppm in the last 12 months versus 279 a year earlier). That is better than the peers' median of 457 ppm, so the scorecard argues its case. On our two dual-sourced parts, however, it is far worse than the rival sup:70610: part:360010 400 vs 56 ppm, part:360012 174 vs 100 ppm.

The EUR 150 flat fee is collected inconsistently: many supplier-caused QNs show EUR 0 recharged. Two recent 8Ds are still open (qn:20005008 on 360010 and qn:20005024 on 360012). Recurring defects (porosity, coating, burr) point to process problems that have not been fixed.

Its prices are high. On part:360010 it charges 14.52 against 12.46 from sup:70610 (+16.5%), with no reduction in three years. On part:360012 it charges 5.60 against 4.91 (+14%). part:360011 at 37.64 is single-sourced. It also receives the larger shares (60% and 70%) despite worse quality.

Our volume outlook is rising on all three parts and the forecasts are shared with the supplier: 360010 574k vs 541k ordered; 360011 208k vs 181k (+15%); 360012 654k vs 600k. Even so, our spend is about 0.7% of its turnover, and it calls our volumes 'not strategic'. More volume is a modest lever but a real one, especially with its second shift idle.

arguments.text: Our framework ends 2026-12-31 and we have already told you individual agreements will not be extended; standard items come from stock at list conditions. The current list prices (14.52 for M12x40, 5.60 for the M12 nut) are what we offer. They are the same prices you have paid all year, not an increase.

The M16x60 bolt has no second source with you. We have supplied it reliably: 92 % on time in the last 12 months. We even cut its price by 2 % for 2026. If you want it to stay on an individual agreement, that has to be worth our while.

Our costs have risen. Fastener producer prices are up 1.7 % in 12 months, manufacturing labour is up 2.7 %, and steel is up 7.3 % since January. Holding prices flat is already a concession, and we lowered the nut by 3.1 % last year.
You have paid late consistently: 90 % of invoices are paid after the due date, on average about 6 days late. We are already financing you beyond the 30-day term.
Our delivery performance is improving. On-time delivery reached 84.1 % and the scorecard rose to 90.6, class A.

weak_points: Leitner is 14 % cheaper on the M12x40 bolt and 12 % cheaper on the nut. Its ppm is far better: 56 vs our 400, and 100 vs our 174. Our own benchmark quotes lost on price in 2025.
Our M16x60 ppm is 390. Complaints recur on coating, porosity and leakage, and qn:20005008 and qn:20005024 have no 8D closure yet.
On-time delivery is still below the 95 % target in the quality agreement. On the M12x40 it is only 76.7 %.
Our second shift has been idle since spring, and we told them we could take additional parts at short notice. We need the volume more than our posture suggests.
The cost drivers are small: fastener PPI is still below its 2023 peak and power prices are sharply down. A real increase is hard to justify.
Hollerau could move its whole quota on the dual-sourced parts to Leitner. That would leave us only the M16 bolt, at roughly 70 kEUR a year.
Auto-renewal: unless we serve notice 60 days before year end, the framework extends by 12 months at current terms. Our committee needs to act before 2026-11-01.
History shows we settle well below what we ask, so they will discount any ask we make.
wants: All three parts bundled, with a higher or 100 % quota on the M12 bolt and nut shifted away from Leitner, to fill the idle shift.
Binding annual volumes at forecast levels (about 574k, 208k and 654k pieces) on a 24-36 month term.
Punctual payment, or a shorter term such as 14-21 days, enforced.
Simple terms with less administrative effort: call-offs consolidated into fewer, larger lots.
Possibly a steel index clause instead of a fixed price on a longer term.
For that package: keep the M16 bolt at 37.64 and move the M12 bolt toward about 13.9-14.2 and the nut toward about 5.4-5.5.
red_lines: No matching of Leitner's 12.46 and 4.91 prices.
No price cut above about 2 % without our pricing committee, and none at all without volume and quota in return.
No extension of the individual agreement at today's terms with today's split quotas.
No higher chargeback per complaint and no hard ppm commitment below about 200 without a price premium.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long relationship. Restate that, under our range refocus, the bespoke framework will not be extended past 2026, and quote list conditions from stock: 14.52, 37.64 and 5.60 for the M16 bolt at current level, with a 7-day validity. Point to rising steel and labour costs and to their late payments. Then leave a door open: we are prepared to keep an individual agreement if Hollerau consolidates the three parts with us at binding, meaningful volume over a longer term and pays on time.

rebuttals.answer: We understand your refocus on key accounts and appreciate that the current prices for the bolt and the nut are unchanged. Under the framework, though, prices are fixed per calendar year, and it extends unless notice is given in time, so we expect to discuss continuation on its terms rather than a switch to list conditions. We would like to make the account worth keeping individually: our shared forecasts show growing volume on all three parts, and we are ready to bundle it and commit to it.

We want to keep it on an individual agreement and to make that worthwhile for you: its forecast volume is clearly above what we ordered over the last year, and we can make it part of a binding, longer-term bundle. The current price is the right basis for that agreement. We would also like to close the recurring complaints on this part together.

We accept that fastener producer prices and labour costs have risen modestly. Weighted by their share of the part cost, they support only a small drift, well below the level that would need your pricing committee. The steel figure covers basic iron and steel, not finished fasteners, and the fastener index already reflects it. Against that, energy prices are far below their earlier level. Holding prices flat in return for more binding volume is a fair balance.

You are right, and we apologise; our payments have too often arrived after the due date. We will commit to punctual payment on the current terms as part of the new agreement, which removes the financing burden you describe without either side reopening the payment terms.
We recognise the clear improvement and the better scorecard, and we thank your team for it. We would like to keep this progress going rather than treat it as grounds for a higher price.

press: You mentioned spare capacity with the second shift on hold; our growing, bundled volume could help fill it if we agree on individual terms.
In past renewals we have always found a balanced result well below the initial ask, and we would like to continue in that spirit.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070650#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 60 days before the end of the calendar year.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement sets the payment terms.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070650#4.1 (payment): Payment: 30 days net. Our standard is 60 days; shorter terms are its benefit.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement sets the delivery terms and the standard lead time.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070650#5.1 (delivery): Delivery DAP; standard lead time 7 days from order.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement includes the quality agreement with its delivery target.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070650#6.1 (quality): The quality agreement applies: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint.

arguments.sentence: Our framework agreement renews only unless either side gives notice.
arguments.note: ctr:4600070650#8.1 (term): Valid from 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31; extends by 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice by 2026-11-01 (still open: a credible exit).
